outcome: No event since 26 January 2024 settles, or moves a bound on, the Bass conjecture for regular schemes of finite type over Z. The in-window items are (a) a finite-field structure theorem that reduces finite generation of Kₘ(X) for smooth projective X over a finite field to a vanishing statement without proving it (Gupta, Krishna and Rathore, arXiv:2603.21000, posted 22 March 2026), and (b) a conditional consequence paper that assumes the motivic form of the conjecture (Hiranouchi and Sugiyama, arXiv:2609.11178, posted 10 September 2026).
problem_asks: The statement (January 2024 wording): 'Bass conjecture on the finite generation of certain algebraic K-groups.' Unpacked: (1) the groups in question are the higher algebraic K-groups Kᵢ(X), for every degree i ≥ 0; (2) the schemes are regular schemes X of finite type over Spec ℤ, which the Wikipedia lead calls 'certain algebraic K-groups'; (3) the claim is that each such group is finitely generated as an abelian group. The article gives four equivalent forms: Kₙ(A) finitely generated for every regular finitely generated ℤ-algebra A; K'ₙ(A) finitely generated for every finitely generated ℤ-algebra A (G-theory); Kₙ(X) for regular X of finite type over ℤ; K'ₙ(X) for any X of finite type over ℤ. So the bullet is a claim about infinitely many groups, over all dimensions of such schemes and all degrees. The motivic refinement (finite generation of H^i_M(X,ℤ(n)) or of higher Chow groups CH^n(X,i)) is not in the bullet; it is a neighbouring, stronger form that appears only as a hypothesis in some later work.

events.what_happened: Quillen, 'Finite generation of the groups Kᵢ of rings of algebraic integers', in Algebraic K-theory I (Springer LNM 341, 1973), pp. 179–198 (DOI 10.1007/BFb0067056, per a bibliographic record seen in search; the volume itself was not opened). The result: Kᵢ(O_F) is finitely generated for every i ≥ 0 and every number field F. The Wikipedia article attributes to Quillen the whole dimension ≤ 1 case, which it describes as rings of integers of number fields and curves over finite fields. In this run the 1973 paper's scope was confirmed only through search snippets, not the paper itself.
events.delivers: Finite generation of Kᵢ(O_F) for all i ≥ 0 and all number fields F, i.e. the conjecture for regular schemes of dimension 1 that are rings of integers (Wikipedia additionally credits normal curves over finite fields, dimension 1). Restricted to dimension ≤ 1.
events.remains: Every regular scheme of finite type over ℤ of dimension ≥ 2, in every degree i ≥ 0. Higher-dimensional cases are what the article calls open.

checked_by.qualification: Working K-theorist; author of the rank spectral sequence construction that extends Quillen's method
checked_by.what_they_did: Digests Quillen's exact-couple method in 'Around Quillen's Theorem A' (arXiv:1108.2441) and in a 2022 seminar abstract; this is an expert exposition of the method, not a verification of a new claim

events.direction: Confirms the conjecture in dimension ≤ 1; it is the known base case and cuts in the conjecture's favour there.

events.what_happened: Known finite generation of CH₀(X), the group of zero-cycles, for regular schemes X of finite type over ℤ. The Wikipedia article attributes this to Bloch, Kato and Saito, and Colliot-Thélène, Soulé and Sansuc, with a later treatment by Kerz and Schmidt. Kerz and Schmidt's 'Covering data and higher dimensional global class field theory' (arXiv:0804.3419, posted 22 April 2008) was seen only as a search snippet, and the snippet did not confirm the CH₀ statement. The Kato–Saito and Colliot-Thélène–Soulé–Sansuc publication years were not established in this run.
events.delivers: Finite generation of CH₀(X) for regular schemes of finite type over ℤ, per the Wikipedia article. This is a zero-cycle (degree-zero Chow) group, not a Kᵢ(X), so it does not settle any K-group in the bullet. It is a related partial result in the motivic/Chow family that the motivic form of the conjecture generalises.
events.remains: All Kᵢ(X) for i ≥ 0 when dim X ≥ 2; the higher Chow groups CH^n(X,i) with i > 0; the K-theory statement itself.
events.direction: Partial result that goes in the conjecture's favour for a different group; it is not a case of the K-theory statement.

events.what_happened: Geisser, 'Finite generation conjectures for cohomology over finite fields', arXiv:1103.5544, single version posted 29 March 2011. It constructs an intermediate cohomology between motivic cohomology and Weil-étale cohomology and states that, using it, the Bass conjecture on finite generation of motivic cohomology and the Beilinson–Tate conjecture on finite generation of Weil-étale cohomology are related. The abstract (opened) claims no unconditional theorem.
events.delivers: A relation between two finiteness conjectures over finite fields. Establishes no finite generation.
events.direction: Neither way: it relates conjectures and proves none of them.

events.what_happened: Gregory, 'Motivic cohomology and algebraic K-theory of some surfaces over finite fields', arXiv:2302.09867, v1 posted 20 February 2023, v2 17 August 2023. Computes the algebraic K-theory of 'some classes of surfaces defined over finite fields', by computing motivic cohomology and the motivic Atiyah–Hirzebruch spectral sequence; an appendix 'slightly enlarge[s] the class of surfaces for which Parshin's conjecture is known' (abstract, opened).
events.delivers: Computes K-groups of a class of surfaces over finite fields. The abstract does not say whether the computed groups are finitely generated. A search snippet of the body said the main theorem assumes that H¹ and H³ vanish, H² is free, and Parshin's conjecture holds for X; this was not verified in the body, and the abstract does not say whether the main computations are conditional.
events.remains: Surfaces outside the stated class; all dimensions ≥ 3; all regular Z-schemes not over finite fields.
events.doubts: Whether the main K-group computations depend on Parshin's conjecture is not established from the abstract. A search snippet says they do; the body was not read to confirm.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture on its class of surfaces; it computes groups and claims no counterexample.

events.what_happened: Gupta, Krishna and Rathore, 'Motivic Cohomology and K-groups of varieties over higher local fields', arXiv:2603.21000 [math.AG], posted 22 March 2026 (single version at the time of fetch, 30 pages). Corollary 1.2 (Corollary 7.10 in the body) concerns smooth projective varieties over a finite field. The introduction says that 'the equivalence of Bass and Parshin's conjectures in higher degrees' is shown there. The abstract's main results concern higher local fields and are not about schemes over ℤ.
events.delivers: For a smooth projective variety X of dimension d over a finite field k and every m ≥ d+1: Kₘ(X) ≅ F ⊕ D, with F finite and D uniquely divisible (Theorem 7.8, stated as unconditional for finite fields; it uses the finiteness of étale cohomology, a Rost–Voevodsky–Weibel / Clausen–Mathew comparison of K-theory with étale K-theory, and a Geisser–Levine vanishing for Kₘ(X, ℤ/p)). Consequently, for m ≥ d+1 the following are equivalent (Corollary 1.2 / 7.10): Kₘ(X) is finitely generated; Kₘ(X) is torsion; Kₘ(X) is a finite group of order prime to p. Theorem 7.8 also says K_d(X)_tor is finite. The paper's Remark 7.9 says that the Bass and Parshin conjectures predict D = 0. The higher-local-field results (quasi-projective varieties over higher local fields have K-groups divisible-by-finite above a suitable degree; finiteness of prime-to-p torsion in higher Chow groups of smooth projective varieties over higher local fields; unique p′-divisibility of the tame reciprocity kernel) concern a different base field and are not statements about ℤ-schemes.
events.remains: Finite generation of Kₘ(X) for smooth projective X over a finite field in each degree m ≥ d+1: this is equivalent to D = 0, which is not proved. Degrees m ≤ d are not resolved beyond finiteness of the torsion in K_d. Regular finite-type ℤ-schemes not over a finite field are untouched. The higher-local-field base is outside the bullet.
events.direction: Toward the conjecture only as a reduction in the finite-field case: finite generation in degrees m ≥ d+1 is shown equivalent to a vanishing (D = 0) that the authors identify with the rational vanishing predicted by Parshin's conjecture. It neither proves nor refutes finite generation in any degree. Finite fields are of finite type over ℤ, so this is an instance of the bullet's class rather than an analogue, but the restriction is large (smooth projective over a finite field, degrees ≥ d+1).

events.what_happened: Hiranouchi and Sugiyama, 'Divisibility and torsion in higher Chow groups over arithmetic fields', arXiv:2609.11178 [math.AG; math.NT], posted 10 September 2026 (single version at the time of fetch). Unconditional results on higher Chow groups CH^{d+i}(X,j) of smooth schemes over finite, local and global fields (divisibility and torsion-freeness in ranges depending on 2i − j). Conditional results for global fields: the introduction says that, under the motivic Bass conjecture, the uniquely divisible group in the range 2i − j ≥ 3 'is also finitely generated', and hence vanishes (citing Proposition 4.18). A search snippet describes Corollary 4.19 as the same conclusion for smooth proper X over a number field with i ≥ 2 and 2i − j ≥ 3, giving CH^{d+i}(X,j) killed by 2; that corollary was not read in the body.
events.delivers: Unconditionally: divisibility and torsion statements for higher Chow groups over finite, local and global fields (abstract, opened). Conditionally on the motivic Bass conjecture for regular schemes of finite type over ℤ: vanishing of a uniquely divisible part of the higher Chow groups over global fields in the range 2i − j ≥ 3 (intro, opened; Proposition 4.18). The conditional form of Corollary 4.19 is reported only through a search snippet. Nothing here establishes finite generation of any Kᵢ(X) over ℤ.
events.remains: Finite generation of Kᵢ(X) for regular X of finite type over ℤ, in all degrees and dimensions; the motivic Bass conjecture itself remains a hypothesis of the conditional results and is not proved.
events.direction: Neither way for the bullet. It draws conditional consequences of the motivic Bass conjecture, which is a stronger form than the K-theory statement (Geisser's note says finite generation of higher Chow groups is 'a slightly stronger statement' than finite generation of K'-groups), and it does not assert that hypothesis.

events.what_happened: Stavrova, 'On the generalized Bass–Quillen conjecture in dimension 2', arXiv:2512.18868 [math.AG; math.KT], posted 21 December 2025. For a regular ring A of dimension ≤ 2 and reductive G with split semisimple derived group, every Zariski-locally trivial principal G-bundle over A[x₁,…,xₙ] is extended from A (abstract, opened).
events.delivers: Projective modules and principal bundles over polynomial rings over regular rings of dimension ≤ 2 (the Bass–Quillen problem). It does not concern finite generation of K-groups. It is a different problem sharing the name 'Bass' and a K-theory tag.
events.remains: The whole bullet. Discarded for this bullet as a different question, with the reason above.
events.direction: Not applicable: a different question, so it neither supports nor cuts against the bullet.

events.what_happened: Balkan and Schreieder, 'Cycle conjectures and birational invariants over finite fields', arXiv:2406.14438, first posted 20 June 2024, latest version 22 December 2025 (abstract, opened). They show that a birational invariant over finite fields vanishes on projective space exactly when the Tate, Beilinson and Grothendieck–Serre 1-semisimplicity conjectures hold for smooth projective varieties over finite fields, and that the conjectures in half the degrees imply them in all degrees.
events.delivers: Equivalences among Tate, Beilinson and semisimplicity conjectures for smooth projective varieties over finite fields. The abstract does not mention the Bass conjecture or finite generation of K-groups. It shares the finite-field setting with the bullet, but it asserts nothing about finite generation.
events.remains: The whole bullet. Discarded as a neighbouring problem.
events.direction: Not applicable: it does not address finite generation of K-groups.

events.what_happened: Lehner, 'The passage from the integral to the rational group ring in algebraic K-theory', arXiv:2110.01413, first posted 4 October 2021; revisions v3 17 March 2025 and v5 16 October 2025 (dates from a search listing, not from opening the arXiv page). It shows the map from reduced K₀(ℤG) to reduced K₀(ℚG) is not always trivial (counterexample QD32 *_Q16 QD32), and gives a computation assuming the Farrell–Jones conjecture. It concerns the strong Bass conjecture for K₀(ℤG), a namesake about Hattori–Stallings traces on group rings.
events.revisions: v1 4 Oct 2021; v3 17 Mar 2025; v5 16 Oct 2025 (search listing)
events.delivers: A group-ring statement about the integral-to-rational K₀ map, which the author says removes one route to the strong Bass conjecture for K₀(ℤG). It is not about finite generation of K-groups of regular ℤ-schemes.
events.remains: The whole bullet. Discarded as a namesake.
events.direction: Not applicable to this bullet: a different problem with the same name.
events.object: A counterexample group, QD32 *_Q16 QD32, to the claim that the integral-to-rational K₀ map is trivial. It is explicit and about group rings, not about this bullet.

events.what_happened: Klein (with Naef, per the ar5iv rendering; the arXiv abstract page lists Klein alone), 'Poincaré complex diagonals and the Bass trace conjecture', arXiv:2208.06289, posted August 2022 (month from the arXiv identifier). Published in Proceedings of the Royal Society of Edinburgh A, 2023, with a corrigendum (DOI 10.1017/prm.2024.144) relabelling 'Corollary F' as 'Conjecture F'. The corrigendum's publication date is given as 18 December 2024 in the PDF and 28 March 2025 online on Cambridge Core. The Bass trace conjecture concerns Hattori–Stallings traces of projective modules over group rings.
events.revisions: arXiv v1 Aug 2022; journal article 2023; corrigendum 2024/2025 (search snippets, not opened)
events.delivers: Results on Poincaré embeddings of diagonal maps and the Reidemeister trace for Poincaré duality spaces. A namesake: the Bass trace conjecture concerns group rings, not finite generation of K-groups.
events.remains: The whole bullet. Discarded as a namesake.

summary: I ran 36 searches (listed verbatim below) and opened the Wikipedia article, the abstracts and as much of the body as the fetch tool returned for both 2026 preprints, the openai/ten-proofs repository, the human audit of the OpenAI results, and several pre-window and neighbouring papers. The Wikipedia article (last edited 12 September 2026) gives four equivalent forms of the conjecture and says only that Quillen proved the dimension ≤ 1 case; it mentions no progress after 2024, so the article does not record any change. Two in-window preprints bear on the bullet. (1) arXiv:2603.21000, Gupta–Krishna–Rathore, 22 March 2026. For smooth projective X over a finite field and m ≥ d+1, its Theorem 7.8 gives Kₘ(X) ≅ F ⊕ D (F finite, D uniquely divisible), and Corollary 1.2 / 7.10 shows finite generation, finiteness with order prime to p, and torsionness are equivalent. The authors call this 'the equivalence of Bass and Parshin's conjectures in higher degrees'. Finite generation therefore reduces to D = 0, which is the vanishing that Parshin's conjecture predicts; it is not proved. I recorded this as a reduction, not a case: it changes which quantity is open but does not settle finite generation in any degree. (2) arXiv:2609.11178, Hiranouchi–Sugiyama, 10 September 2026. Its unconditional results are divisibility and torsion statements for higher Chow groups over finite, local and global fields. Its global-field consequences are stated under the motivic Bass conjecture: the introduction says that under that hypothesis the uniquely divisible group in the range 2i − j ≥ 3 is also finitely generated and so vanishes (citing Proposition 4.18). I read that sentence in the introduction, not Proposition 4.18 or Corollary 4.19, which the fetch did not reach. The paper does not prove the hypothesis. Pre-window background (Quillen 1973, Geisser 2011, Gregory 2023, the zero-cycle result for CH₀) is recorded as events; the zero-cycle result is a different group, and its year was not established. Four namesake or neighbouring papers (Stavrova 2025 on Bass–Quillen; Balkan–Schreieder 2024/2025 on finite-field Tate/Beilinson conjectures; Lehner 2021 on group rings; Klein–Naef 2022 on the Bass trace conjecture) are recorded as discards with reasons. A note on the earlier record: data/mark_2026-09-22/deepdive/out/bass-conjecture.json reports no event and does not mention arXiv:2603.21000, which was posted before that run. The judging pass should reconcile the two. AI: I found no source connecting any AI system to this bullet. OpenAI's Astra announcement (1 August 2026) included ten results with Lean certificates; the repository README lists sphere packing, codes, non-sofic groups, Connes's rigidity conjecture, the permanent, quantum parallel repetition, the closest vector problem, Ehrhart's volume conjecture, multicolour Ramsey numbers and extremal-number conjectures, and none is in K-theory or about finite generation. The human audit (arXiv:2608.14673) names only Connes's rigidity conjecture among the results it names. Other AI hits (AlphaEvolve and Gemini Deep Think on the finite-field Kakeya problem, the 'Gödel test' of GPT-5 on combinatorial optimisation, a Peking University commutative-algebra result) are unrelated. Several aggregator articles claim AI results on other problems (Jacobian conjecture, Navier–Stokes, Unique Games); I did not research them because they fall outside this bullet, and I could not verify them. Close call: whether the finite-field reduction in (1) counts as a case of the bullet. Finite fields are of finite type over ℤ, so the instances are the bullet's own, but the result does not decide finite generation for any of them.
competing_reading: The strongest case for counting (1) as progress: Theorem 7.8 is a genuine structure theorem for the bullet's own instances (smooth projective over finite fields). It shows that the only possible obstruction to finite generation in degrees ≥ d+1 is a uniquely divisible part, identifies that part exactly, and proves the equivalence with torsion-ness and finite order prime to p. On this reading a named quantity has moved (the divisible part is now the unique open piece) even though the problem stays open. Against it: no finite generation is proved for any degree, the divisible part may be nonzero, the reduction is standard in form (finiteness of étale cohomology plus known vanishing), and the bullet asks about all regular schemes of finite type over ℤ, a far larger class. For (2), the strongest reading is that conditional corollaries under the motivic Bass conjecture are evidence the authors regard the conjecture as plausible. That is an opinion about the hypothesis, not a result about the bullet.
what_would_settle_it: (a) A proof that D = 0 (equivalently that Kₘ(X) is finite or finitely generated) for smooth projective X over finite fields in some degree m ≥ d+1, or any finite-generation statement for a Z-scheme not over a finite field. (b) The body of arXiv:2609.11178 around Proposition 4.18 and Corollary 4.19, confirming the hypothesis and conclusion verbatim. (c) The full text of arXiv:2603.21000 to confirm that Corollary 1.2 contains no unstated hypothesis and that the acknowledgements name no AI system. (d) Citing or critical papers after October 2026 on either preprint, which would show whether they were checked. (e) The year of the CH₀ result and the Kerz–Schmidt paper's actual scope, which are unverified here. (f) An AI-attribution statement in the body of any post-2024 paper on this bullet; none has been found.

incomplete: (1) arXiv:2603.21000: the HTML body was read in two chunks (about 100,000 characters, then the section on finite fields), and the total length is about 171,000 characters, so the final portion, including the acknowledgements, was not read. The PDF was unreadable through the fetch tool. The ai.none_found finding for this event is therefore provisional: nothing in what I read names a system, but the acknowledgements and contribution statement were not checked. (2) arXiv:2609.11178: the HTML body was read in two chunks (about 100,000 characters, then part of the next), and the total is about 137,000 characters. Proposition 4.18 and Corollary 4.19 were not reached; the conditional statement is verified only through the introduction's sentence and a search snippet of Corollary 4.19, which is therefore not verified. Its acknowledgements were not read either, so its ai.none_found is provisional too. (3) Quillen's 1973 scope is confirmed only through search snippets and Wikipedia; the Murayama notes returned HTTP 403. (4) The CH₀ event has no date: the Kato–Saito and Colliot-Thélène–Soulé–Sansuc years and the Kerz–Schmidt CH₀ claim were not established. (5) Gregory (2023) conditionality is reported from a search snippet, not from the body. (6) The Lehner and Klein–Naef entries use dates and revisions from search listings and snippets, not from opened pages. (7) No arXiv listing for the period after 10 September 2026 was read, and the search index covers recent postings poorly, so a preprint posted in late September or October 2026 could be missing. (8) The publication status of the two 2026 preprints was not checked beyond their arXiv pages. (9) No citation counts or later commentary were checked, beyond search queries for them, which found nothing.
